title: Roadmap / Launch Readiness - Postmortem
summary: Internal postmortem and launch-readiness review for Q4 roadmap items. Focus on incident from 2026-12-03, rollout cadence, outstanding infra items (KV cache warmup, autoscale flakiness), docs and developer experience follow-ups. Decided on remediation priorities, tentative dates for fixes, and owners for launch checklist items.
topics: KV cache and prefix caching behavior
Autoscaling policy and burst capacity flakiness
Rollout / canary strategy for Dedicated customers

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-10 10:00 UTC
Duration: 1:15
Attendees: Maya, Liam, Sofia, Aaron, Elena, Tom, Jules, Priya, Diego

Summary (auto): quick notes - postmortem and readiness items, owners assigned.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): okay thanks everyone for joining, we'll run about an hour, hour fifteen, we're doing a postmortem on the 12-03 degradation and then tie into launch readiness for the q4 items, um quick check, any blockers to starting?
00:18 Speaker 2 (Liam): no blockers here, I can share the timeline, I pulled the oncall logs and the autoscaler had two back-to-back failures which exacerbated the queue.
00:35 Speaker 3 (Sofia): yeah and to add the KV cache didn't warm up as expected, the prefix caching behavior was slower than our assumptions, so when nodes scaled up the cold-start penalty was bigger. sometimes the transcript says K V cache cause of the speech model, sorry for the noise.
00:52 Speaker 1 (Maya): mm-hmm, okay can we walk through the incident timeline quickly? Liam do you want to run that?
01:00 Speaker 2 (Liam): yeah timeline — at 03:12 we saw increased latency on hosted, at 03:14 autoscaler spun up, at 03:18 another scale event failed due to scheduling churn on the pool and we lost a KV cache boundary, at 03:22 traffic spiked and degraded further. by 03:30 we were throttling requests to preserve SLO.
01:28 Speaker 4 (Jules): quick question, was the scheduling churn related to reserved capacity or a cloud provider transient?
01:35 Speaker 2 (Liam): looks like a combination; reserved capacity nodes were fine but the burst pool experienced a provisioning lag, the AZ reported degraded API responses, so the scheduler retried.
01:52 Speaker 5 (Tom): and the KV cache issue — is that a code regression or an operational parameter?
02:00 Speaker 3 (Sofia): initial look is operational—cache TTLs and prefix eviction thresholds are tuned for steady-state not fast burst, so when a cold node comes online it takes a long time to populate hot prefixes, we also saw some deserialize overhead on the load path.
02:20 Speaker 1 (Maya): okay that matches the customer reports. Let's map out remediations: short-term and medium-term. short-term fixes we can do before the end of month?
02:34 Speaker 6 (Priya): for QA, we need a deterministic regression harness that simulates burst traffic and cold nodes, otherwise we won't catch the warmup regressions.
02:44 Speaker 2 (Liam): agreed, I'll own the harness plus a follow-up smoke run against staging.
03:01 Speaker 7 (Diego): also recommend adding a synthetic test that hits the KV cache prefixes specifically during scale events. it should live in the canary gate.
03:15 Speaker 3 (Sofia): for infra, short-term patch is to pre-warm common prefixes in new nodes and add quicker eviction on low-value keys. medium term is re-architecting the warmup path to stream missing prefixes from a central prefetcher.
03:40 Speaker 1 (Maya): any risk to shipping the pre-warm patch before the canary?
03:46 Speaker 3 (Sofia): low risk, we've run local microbenchmarks, but we need staging throughput tests to validate.
04:05 Speaker 2 (Liam): autoscaler fix — root cause seems to be retry backoff not adapting to scheduling failures, so we should adjust backoff policy and add circuit-breaker for repeated provisioning errors.
04:25 Speaker 5 (Tom): make sure any autoscaler tuning doesn't break Dedicated customers with pinned capacity.
04:33 Speaker 2 (Liam): yeah we'll gate by customer tier; reserve the change to burst pool only.
04:40 Speaker 1 (Maya): good. next: rollout strategy. we need canary windows, rollback thresholds, and an exec signoff for Dedicated customers.
04:55 Speaker 6 (Priya): propose a two-phase canary: internal canary to 10% traffic then 24h observation then Dedicated canary with one customer for 48h.
05:12 Speaker 1 (Maya): sounds reasonable. who tracks the canary checklist?
05:18 Speaker 4 (Jules): SRE can own the checklist with Product verifying the metrics.
05:25 Speaker 3 (Sofia): we should add explicit KV cache warmup verification to that checklist, and a smoke test that validates tail latency under sudden 2x load.
05:40 Speaker 7 (Diego): on the QA side we'll add the regression matrix entry and schedule two full runs before the canary window.
06:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): docs and dev experience — Aaron?
06:05 Speaker 8 (Aaron): I'll update the developer onboarding snippets with the new cache warmup notes, and add a troubleshooting section for the autoscaler signals, also plan to add a short runbook for the oncall to follow during scale events.
06:20 Speaker 5 (Tom): also we need to lock down the launch readiness checklist; include security signoffs, SOC2 evidence, and the customer communication plan.
06:30 Speaker 1 (Maya): security folks already reviewed SOC2 artifacts last week but we'll double-check the audit logs retention and KMS integration notes before we ship.
06:42 Speaker 3 (Sofia): small note: KMS rotation tests — we had one slip in staging where rotation caused a transient auth failure; needs a test in the CI pipeline.
06:55 Speaker 2 (Liam): ok putting that on the list.
07:05 Speaker 1 (Maya): timeline proposals — we want to hit GA-ish by end of january; with the canary windows set for week of 2026-12-28 and final verification in early january it feels tight but doable.
07:20 Speaker 6 (Priya): QA calendar wise, allow two weeks for regression runs and one week for fixes, so that puts go/no-go around 2027-01-10.
07:35 Speaker 1 (Maya): noted. let's do a quick round-robin for owners and due dates.
07:45 Speaker 2 (Liam): I'll produce the RCA and the autoscaler PR by 12-17.
07:52 Speaker 3 (Sofia): infra patch to pre-warm and warmup benchmark by 12-20.
07:58 Speaker 8 (Aaron): docs and runbook updates 12-15.
08:05 Speaker 7 (Diego): QA regression matrix and two smoke runs by 12-18.
08:15 Speaker 1 (Maya): ok and we'll reconvene next Thursday for a status checkpoint.
08:22 Speaker 4 (Jules): quick question — do we want to notify Dedicated customers proactively about the plan?
08:30 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes send a brief note after we have the canary dates, mention mitigations and that we're scheduling a Dedicated-only canary. Aaron can draft the customer comms.
08:40 Speaker 8 (Aaron): will do.
08:45 Speaker 1 (Maya): any other items?
08:50 Speaker 5 (Tom): just to flag competitor context — AptitudeAI rolled out a similar warmup hack and saw transient regressions, we should watch their notes but not copy blindly.
08:58 Speaker 1 (Maya): great. we'll close with recap — owners and dates in the doc, status check next Thursday, and action items assigned. thanks all.
09:10 Speaker 2 (Liam): thanks everyone.
09:15 Meeting end.
